title: Transforming a text into a new form
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:15Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No bank point teaches retelling a text in another form or from another character's view; the closest, intertextual connections, only mentions retold stories as links between texts, and the others cover interpreting, text forms, comparison and values.

draft.title: Transforming a text into a new form
card: To transform a text is to retell it in a new form, such as a letter, diary entry, poem or speech. You can also change who tells it.
the features of the new form shape the retelling. A diary entry is private and personal, while a news report is formal and factual.
telling the story through another character shows events the original left out. That character's feelings and opinions replace the first narrator's.
A transformation keeps the main events of the original but changes what readers notice and feel. The writer chooses which details to keep, drop or add.
draft.remember: A transformation keeps the story's events but changes what readers notice and feel.

a.q: A student retells a fairy tale as a letter written by the wolf to a friend. What is the main effect of this change?
opts: Readers see events through the wolf's feelings and opinions
Readers get a neutral, factual account of what happened
Readers learn nothing new, because the events are the same
Readers see the same viewpoint as the original narrator
a.why: Moving to the wolf's viewpoint replaces the original narrator's opinions with the wolf's, so readers notice different things. The events can stay the same while the feelings change, so the effect is not nothing.
a.clue: Whose feelings and opinions now shape the story?

b.q: Priya retells a story of a shipwreck, first told by an officer in a formal report, as a diary entry by a young deckhand. Which change would you expect in her version?
opts: More personal fear and detail the officer left out
The same formal tone and the same viewpoint
A list of facts with no feelings shown
New main events that contradict the original story
b.why: A diary is private and personal, and the deckhand sees the wreck differently from the officer, so personal feelings and missing details appear. Changing the main events would be a new story, not a transformation.
b.clue: Think about what a private diary and a different narrator each add.

a.best: Readers see events through the wolf's feelings and opinions

b.best: More personal fear and detail the officer left out
